query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: A single-stage thermal aging treatment that induces fine, coherent secondary precipitates along the lamellar interfaces can improve the alloy’s strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion performance for fastener applications.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in a uniform, fine lamellar state.
generation.intervention: Perform a carefully calibrated thermal aging treatment (e.g., holding the alloy at an optimized elevated temperature for a set duration) to promote controlled precipitation of a secondary intermetallic phase.
generation.conditions: Simulated fastener environments with extreme temperature fluctuations (approx. –50°C to 500°C), long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive exposures.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of fine, coherent precipitates at or near lamellar interfaces that are dispersed uniformly throughout the microstructure.
generation.mechanism: The precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding, thereby increasing yield strength and slowing creep; they may also stabilize the microstructure against coarsening under thermal cycling and provide localized corrosion resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-cast fine lamellar state, the aged alloy is expected to display enhanced yield strength and ductility (potential improvement on the order of 10–20% based on anticipated precipitate hardening effects) along with improved creep resistance and lower corrosion rates under the test conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated, uniform fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy with strength and plasticity below industrial application requirements for fasteners.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are anticipated within the operational range relevant for fasteners (temperature roughly –50°C to 500°C, continuous load conditions, and moderate corrosive environments). Outside these boundaries, precipitate coarsening or embrittlement may negate benefits.
generation.uncertainty: Exact aging parameters (temperature, duration) for optimal precipitate formation remain to be determined, and the balance between strengthening and avoiding embrittlement under cyclic temperature fluctuations requires experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy specimens: one set subjected to the proposed thermal aging treatment and one control set left in its as-cast state. Expose both sets to laboratory simulations of extreme temperature cycling, sustained mechanical loading (including creep tests), and corrosive environments. Use microscopy to confirm precipitate presence and distribution.
measurements: Tensile tests to measure yield strength and ductility
Creep rate measurements at room temperature under constant stress
Electrochemical corrosion tests (e.g., impedance spectroscopy, potentiodynamic polarization)
Microstructural characterization (SEM/TEM) to verify precipitate size, distribution, and coherence
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal aging does not result in at least a 10% improvement in mechanical properties (strength and ductility) and does not demonstrate improved creep or lower corrosion rates compared to the as-cast condition, or if adverse effects such as embrittlement are observed, the hypothesis is falsified.
